ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal corporate transparency statutes are the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including sections 2.1 and 21.1 to 21.303 concerning individuals with significant control, and Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, together with its implementing regulation, the Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, r. 2. Canadian AML/CFT obligations are principally governed by the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. An ordinary software corporation is generally not a reporting entity solely because it develops or sells software; obligations may arise if it conducts money services, payment, foreign-exchange, virtual-currency, lending, securities, or other regulated activities.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all proposed directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, authorized signatories, agents, and controlling persons before incorporation and before onboarding with banks or payment processors. Screening should cover Canadian sanctions and terrorist listings under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, Criminal Code terrorist listings, and related regulations; United Nations Security Council lists; OFAC sanctions lists where United States nexus, dollar clearing, United States persons, or United States technology is involved; and relevant foreign sanctions lists based on transaction exposure. Conduct politically exposed person and head-of-international-organization screening under the PCMLTFA framework where a reporting entity is involved. Maintain documented identity resolution, adverse-media review, escalation, false-positive clearance, sanctions blocking, enhanced due diligence, and periodic rescreening. Do not treat OFAC as universally binding Canadian law, but assess it contractually and for United States nexus risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), online services portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/; for a federal corporation, Corporations Canada online filing centre: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec corporation carrying on business in Quebec must comply with the Charter of the French Language, CQLR, c. C-11. The declared name must be French or satisfy the applicable statutory and administrative conditions for a non-French name. A French version is generally required for public and commercial use in Quebec, subject to limited statutory exceptions. English or foreign-language names may require supporting explanations and may be rejected if confusing, generic, misleading, contrary to public order, or unavailable. Transliteration does not cure a conflict or eliminate French-language obligations. A federal corporation carrying on business in Quebec must also comply with Quebec language legislation and may use a corporate name in English, French, or both under the Canada Business Corporations Act, subject to Quebec use and registration requirements.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a regulated financial, insurance, professional, educational, or governmental status
Words that falsely suggest a connection with the Crown, the Government of Canada, the Government of Quebec, a municipality, or an existing legal person
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Treat 30 days as the internal filing target required by this dossier and verify the current REQ certificate terms at filing; Quebec and federal name-search or reservation documents may have different administrative validity periods, commonly up to 90 days depending on the service. Obtain a current name search or reservation, retain the search report, and file the incorporation or constitutive amendment before expiry. If rejected, obtain the written reason, compare the proposed name against the statutory criteria and existing registrations, submit a revised name or supporting evidence through the REQ or Corporations Canada portal, and request administrative reconsideration or correction from the responsible registry unit. If the decision remains disputed, consult the applicable Quebec administrative review or judicial review procedure and observe statutory limitation periods. A rejection appeal does not authorize use of the rejected name.
recommended_clearance_sequence: Search the REQ and Corporations Canada databases for identical, confusingly similar, translated, and phonetic names
Search Canadian trademarks through the Canadian Trademarks Database and review domain names and major platform identifiers
Check French-language compliance, misleading-industry implications, and regulated-word restrictions
Obtain a Quebec name reservation or federal NUANS-based name approval as applicable
Reserve matching French, English, abbreviated, and domain-name variants where commercially necessary
Complete a final conflict and sanctions check immediately before signing incorporation documents

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Quebec is mandatory for a Quebec corporation, and a federal corporation carrying on business in Quebec must maintain the registered office and registration required by the applicable corporate and enterprise-registration statutes. A commercial virtual office may be acceptable if it is a genuine address capable of receiving official service and maintaining required corporate records, but a mail-forwarding-only address, undisclosed nominee office, or address disconnected from actual management may be rejected by banks, payment processors, tax authorities, or licensing and privacy reviewers. For remote-support software and unattended machine telemetry software, no sector-specific premises licence is ordinarily required. The company should nevertheless maintain credible Canadian operational substance, including accessible records, responsible officers, contractual capacity, privacy governance, cybersecurity controls, and evidence of actual business activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No published statutory probability exists. For a low-risk software corporation with consistent registry, tax, banking, privacy, and beneficial-ownership information, unannounced physical inspection risk is generally low. A reasonable compliance planning assessment is below 5% annually in ordinary conditions, not a legal safe harbour; the risk increases materially if the registered office is a mailbox, filings are inconsistent, directors or beneficial owners cannot be verified, tax returns are missing, complaints arise, or payment activity resembles money services or regulated financial activity.
substance_and_operational_controls: Maintain a Quebec registered office capable of receiving legal service and government correspondence
Maintain corporate registers, beneficial ownership records, director consents, resolutions, and shareholder records
Identify the actual place of central management and control for Canadian tax-residency analysis
Document software ownership, source-code control, licensing rights, contractor arrangements, and data-processing roles

Implement privacy compliance under the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act and Quebec's Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR, c. P-39.1, including breach and governance controls where applicable
Assess Law 25 requirements, cross-border transfer controls, privacy impact assessments, and service-provider contracts for personal information
Confirm whether remote-access functionality creates cybersecurity, telecommunications, export-control, sanctions, or customer-contract restrictions
Obtain written bank and payment-processor approval for the intended Stripe and Paddle business model

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), C.Q.L.R. c. S-31.1 (QBCA), ss. 21–25 (articles/certificate), s. 110 (directors), s. 116 (officers); Regulation respecting the Business Corporations Act, C.Q.L.R. c. S-31.1, r. 1; alternative federal regime available under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, with extra-provincial registration in Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, C.Q.L.R. c. P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Quebec Business Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) filed electronically under QBCA s. 21 through the REQ online transactional filing service.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Québec business corporation. The issued share capital is fixed by the incorporator/board; no escrow account, government deposit, or proof-of-funds requirement applies at formation. Shares may be issued with or without par value and consideration may be paid in money, property, or past services. Corporate existence begins on the certificate date (QBCA s. 23).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the articles of incorporation and the certificate of incorporation issued under section 23 of the Business Corporations Act (Québec) are ratified and confirmed; THAT the by-laws of the corporation governing the conduct of its affairs are hereby adopted; THAT the corporation issue and allot one thousand common shares to the subscriber named in the securities register upon payment of the consideration approved by the incorporator; THAT the registered office of the corporation is established at [address], Montreal, Province of Quebec; THAT [Name] be appointed President/Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each authorized to open and operate banking accounts; and THAT the corporate seal be adopted and the statutory minute book be maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ — Quebec Business Registry, Name Research and Reservation Window (online at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-research request through the REQ 'Nom d'entreprise' online service to certify that the proposed corporate name (e.g., 'Remote Screen Share Technologies Inc.') is lawful, distinctive, and not confusing with existing registrations under QBCA s. 51 and the legal publicity regime. The resulting name declaration (déclaration pour recherche de nom) is attached to the articles. If no name is adopted, a numeric/industrial designation may be used.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and reverse-name variant list
Incorporator contact information and declaration
REQ name research request form and declaration of lawful use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ queries the name, file a written memorandum distinguishing the proposed business activities from prior registrations, or elect an alternate distinctive name or numeric designation within 15 days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ — Direction de l'immatriculation, online Articles of Incorporation transaction service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the electronic Statuts de constitution under QBCA s. 21. Enter the adopted corporate name, the registered office physical address in Québec, the head office mailing address, the number and category of directors (minimum one natural person), and the share capital structure (e.g., an unlimited number of common shares without par value). Pay the C$350 filing fee by credit card or Interac. The transaction generates a confirmation receipt with a registry file number. Notarization is not mandatory; electronic authentication by the declarant is accepted.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ electronic articles form
REQ name research declaration
Applicant/incorporator attestation and appointment
Physical Quebec registered office address confirmation
First directors list with names, addresses, and consent declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of correction or deficiency, submit the corrected electronic filing and pay any additional duty within the 10-to-30-day cure window; repeated refusal may be cured by filing amended articles under QBCA s. 22.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: REQ — Office of the Registrar and Publication Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, REQ issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and simultaneously registers the enterprise (immatriculation), generating the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec). Verify the certificate data, affix it to the corporate minute book, and publish or retain the attestation as evidence of legal existence. The registration also triggers the REQ initial publicity disclosure of directors.
required_dossiers: Filing confirmation receipt and proof of fee payment
Approved articles of incorporation as filed
Director consent declarations
Identity attestation of the filing applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or registration is refused or contains a registry disclosure error, apply for rectification under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (C.Q.L.R. c. P-44.1) within 30 days and refile the corrected declaration electronically.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board of Directors Meeting and Organizational Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation board of directors, administered by corporate legal counsel at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or obtain unanimous written resolutions signed by all directors in lieu of a meeting (QBCA ss. 345–347). Adopt By-Law No. 1, subscribe and allot the initial share capital to the incorporator, confirm the registered office address, approve the corporate seal and share certificate forms, appoint the officers (President/CEO, Secretary, CFO), fix the fiscal year-end, approve the minute book, and authorize the opening of corporate bank accounts.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes or written resolution
By-Law No. 1
Securities register and share certificate stubs
Director office attestations and officer acceptance forms
Registered office lease or occupancy evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director's consent is invalid or quorum is defective, re-execute the resolutions with the unanimous written consent of all then-serving directors and record the date of the corrective execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax and Regulatory Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec — enterprise registration and QST services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Business Number (BN) with the CRA and obtain a GST/HST program account where taxable sales exceed C$30,000 annually; register with Revenu Québec for the QST, source deductions, and provincial payroll accounts; file the employer attestation with the CNESST for occupational health and safety coverage; obtain the municipal occupancy or business permit for the physical premises; and submit the director identity declaration update to REQ through the REQ updated declaration form.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NEQ
First Board Resolution appointing officers
Registered office lease or proof of Québec establishment
Director identification and residency declarations
CRA RC1 form and Revenu Québec LM-1 registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec queries the registration, provide the certificate, office evidence, and officer attestation within 10 business days; reasonable-cause relief from late-registration penalties may be requested under voluntary disclosure procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing board applies to software publishing and computer programming (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210). General regulatory oversight is exercised by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for commercial registry and by the municipal land-use and building department (e.g., Ville de Montréal — Bureau des permis) for physical premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral statutory operating license is mandated for the remote screen-sharing and IoT telemetry software business. The applicable operational permits are the municipal business occupancy permit (permis d'exploitation commerciale) and the REQ enterprise registration certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category D: software, information technology, and office-based projects are not listed in the mandatory EIA declaration schedule under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (C.Q.L.R. c. Q-2, r. 23); no preliminary study, full EIA report, or ministerial authorization is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No air emission or VOC limits apply to non-manufacturing IT operations; office sanitary effluent discharges to municipal sewerage under the applicable municipal by-law; electronic waste (servers, monitors, IoT devices) must be recovered and recycled through a recognized program under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of products by enterprises (C.Q.L.R. c. Q-2, r. 46.1); battery waste must comply with the Québec Battery Regulation (C.Q.L.R. c. Q-2, r. 8.1).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certificate issued by the local fire prevention service under the Fire Safety Act (C.Q.L.R. c. S-2.3.1), confirming means of egress, alarms, and extinguishers; CNESST employer registration and occupational first-aid compliance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety; office structural load adequacy confirmed against the Québec Construction Code; no industrial clearance or special environmental authorization is required for pure software or remote-support operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and federal income tax administration, operating through the 'My Business Account' portal; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), Quebec corporation tax, and Quebec payroll remittances, operating through the Revenu Québec online portal with CléNuméro/NEO.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation with Quebec nexus must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST program account by filing CRA Form RC3486 (Application for Registration for the GST/HST) via CRA's non-resident registration channel or My Business Account. Supporting documents include articles of incorporation, foreign registry extract, proof of director identity, and a completed RC59 (Authorization or Cancellation of Authorization of a Representative) where a Canadian representative is used. For Quebec, the same entity registers with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial corporate accounts using Form LM-1 (Application for Registration for the GST/HST and QST) or the online Business Registration service. The federal TIN is the 15-character Business Number program account (e.g., 123456789 RC0001); Quebec assigns a distinct QST registration file number. Registration must be completed before the first taxable supply is made in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canada/Quebec business corporation is a separate taxable person on its worldwide income; no pass-through or check-the-box eligibility for corporations; non-resident shareholders are additionally subject to Part XIII withholding tax on dividends.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box pass-through election for corporations. Available statutory elections include ITA s. 85 rollover on incorporation or asset transfers, ITA s. 86 share-forexchange elections, ITA s. 216 net-income election for non-resident rental suppliers, ITA s. 219 branch tax elections, capital dividend account elections under ITA s. 83(2), and fiscal period elections under ITA s. 249.1. Hybrid mismatch integrity rules in ITA s. 18.6, effective 1 July 2022, apply deduction/non-inclusion and imported-mismatch adjustments without elective opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST at federal 5%) administered by CRA, combined with Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ at 9.975%) administered by Revenu Québec; combined nominal rate for taxable remote software and support supplies in Quebec is 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The GST/HST small supplier threshold is CAD 30,000 of worldwide gross taxable supplies (current calendar quarter plus the preceding four quarters) under ETA s. 228(3) and Schedule IX; the QST threshold is likewise CAD 30,000 under the Quebec Taxation Act. For non-resident suppliers of remote desktop access and IoT telemetry software, the 1 July 2021 place-of-supply rules apply: a non-resident must register for GST/HST and QST once the threshold is exceeded, and registration is required earlier where the non-resident fails to establish small-supplier status or supplies services to consumers located in Quebec through certain digital platform arrangements. B2B supplies of software access to GST/HST registrants for their commercial activities are generally zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, government API validation, or digital stamping for invoices. Electronic invoices are accepted if they contain the prescribed GST/HST/QST information under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec's parallel rules. Revenu Québec has announced a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing framework based on PEPPOL BIS 3.0, with voluntary adoption in 2025, phased mandatory deployment for large businesses expected from 2026, and broader SME rollout thereafter; the CRA has no equivalent federal mandate. Taxpayers must retain machine-readable sales, export, and remittance documentation for at least six years for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST zero-rating applies to (i) supplies of goods exported from Canada where the goods are exported by the supplier in accordance with ETA s. 170(2), generally within 60 days of delivery; (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person where the service is not in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada and is not for use by the recipient in Canada (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7); and (iii) intangible property, including software access, remote desktop session connectivity, and IoT telemetry data feeds, supplied to non-residents for use exclusively outside Canada. Quebec QST zero-rating rules mirror the GST framework. For remote screen-share and unattended-machine telemetry services, the contract must evidence the non-resident recipient and the foreign destination of the benefit; the supplier must retain proof of the recipient's non-resident status and documentation that the service was not consumed in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (B13A and Canadian Export Reporting System CERS transmission) for any exported hardware or goods; for pure software services, the service agreement governs
Bill of lading or airway waybill evidencing physical export of goods, when applicable
Commercial invoice and master service agreement identifying the foreign recipient and the remote screen-share/IoT telemetry supply
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank statement proving payment received from outside Canada
Non-resident status evidence (certificate of corporate residence, foreign tax residency certificate, or comparable due-diligence record)
Destination and use statement from the customer declaring that the software service is consumed exclusively outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec rigorously audit export zero-rating claims for documentary completeness; missing export, non-resident, or remittance evidence can cause the supply to be reclassified as taxable, triggering unremitted tax, arrears interest, and penalties. Under the Excise Tax Act, false or omitted statements on returns attract a penalty of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax at issue (ETA s. 280), with additional penalties for failure to register or remit (ETA s. 285). The normal four-year reassessment window is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful neglect is established. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion is available under Criminal Code s. 380, with repayment, fines, and imprisonment. Revenu Québec has parallel audit, penalty, interest, and security-demand powers under the Quebec Tax Administration Act; transfer pricing review under ITA s. 247 may additionally adjust revenue allocations where export invoicing and foreign remittance do not reflect arm's length economics. While the Excise Tax Act does not prescribe a fixed foreign-exchange repatriation date, the 180-day benchmark is adopted in this compliance framework for documentary continuity and audit defensibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary authority; no dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration; exchange control and investment regulation are administered by the Department of Finance Canada and the Investment Review Division of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada under the Investment Canada Act; banking and payment-system supervision is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Bank of Canada under the Payment Clearing and Settlement Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange controls in Canada; the Foreign Exchange Control Orders have been repealed. Dividends, royalties, and branch remittances are subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory, possibly reduced under treaty), but no prior administrative approval for profit repatriation is required. Cross-border transactions exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC, and all clearing banks are required to conduct AML/ATF due diligence on value chains.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada maintains no mandatory surrender or conversion regime for export proceeds. Export receipts may be freely retained in Canadian dollars or any foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts. There are no statutory deadlines or conversion ratios. Companies may use export proceeds directly for payments, reinvestment, or repatriation, subject only to ordinary reporting thresholds under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments surveys.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) are not authorized under the Bank Act to accept deposits in Canada or to act as principal treasury custodians. They may only provide auxiliary payment facilities after registration as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC, with full PCMLTFA compliance. They cannot serve as the primary corporate settlement bank or clearing hub for a Quebec-incorporated entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorized director or signatory is generally required by Schedule I banks for initial corporate account opening, especially where the beneficial owners are non-resident. Some financial institutions permit fully remote onboarding through secure video interview, digital identity verification using Canadian credit files, and notarized corporate documents. However, for a newly incorporated Quebec business corporation, in-branch or video interview is effectively mandatory; strict enhanced due diligence applies to non-resident shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director domiciled in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial ownership attestation, corporate registry extract from Registraire des entreprises du Québec, identity documents with verification, source of wealth file, board resolutions, adverse media search result, organizational chart proving transparent chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction flow inconsistent with stated software-as-a-service business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, product technical documentation, live website/app description, customer contracts, pipeline invoices, proof of software subscription revenue, internal AML policies, and a clear cash-flow projection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident majority shareholding without clear economic substance in Canada
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Articles and certificate of incorporation, minute book, register of directors, shareholders' register, lease agreement for registered office in Quebec, substance documentation (employees, payroll, CRA/Revenu Québec filings), transfer pricing policy, functional analysis, and bank reference letters from parent jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid or unusually large early-stage capital injection prompting source-of-funds concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolutions approving equity issuance, subscription agreement, investor KYC packs, audited financial statements (if available), source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations, bank statements showing originating account, and legal opinion on the transaction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the entity's Canadian Schedule I bank account. Remittance information (Field 70) should unambiguously state 'Share capital contribution' or 'Equity injection' and reference the corporate entity name. The bank will require supporting documentation, including a board resolution authorizing share issuance, subscription agreement, proof of beneficial ownership, and source of funds. CAD conversion occurs at prevailing market rates by the receiving Canadian bank. For investments exceeding Investment Canada Act thresholds, pre-closing notification to Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada may be required. All funds above CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are effected through SWIFT MT103/MT202 for wire transfers, domestic CAD clearing via Lynx or the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS), USD clearing through CHIPS/ACH, and Commercial Letters of Credit for physical-goods trade. For software licensing, subscription fees, intercompany royalties, and service fees, wire transfer with appropriate CRA withholding tax forms (e.g., NR4, NR301, and Quebec RD-QL) is standard. No capital-control approval is needed, but all cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by the financial institution to FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (fixed-date and window forwards)
FX futures traded on recognized exchanges

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Update (Annual Declaration of Update; Déclaration annuelle de mise à jour), including beneficial-owner attestation and current director/senior-officer particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's registration in the Quebec enterprise register, each calendar year (annual date regime under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid annual fee posts as an arrearage on the register; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes administrative strike-off (dissolution) by REQ; restoration requires a Quebec Superior Court order and payment of arrear fees plus interest; statutory fines for a legal person may reach CAD 2,500 for knowingly false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) — applicable if the entity is incorporated federally and extra-provincially registered in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the corporation's incorporation under the CBCA; an immediate update is also required upon any change of registered office and director names or addresses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary late fee is assessed for a single missed year; however, failure to file annual returns for three consecutive years empowers the Director to dissolve the corporation under CBCA s. 212; revival remains possible within five years under s. 209 but requires the corporation to cure all arrears and pay revival duties, creating a period of legal incapacity, contract and asset-vesting risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based statutory audit threshold applies to a private Quebec business corporation. An independent auditor is mandatory only if the corporation is a reporting issuer (public) or has not obtained the unanimous written consent of all shareholders to waive the audit (CBCA s. 163; QBCA s. 224). Any shareholder or group holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares may requisition an audit or re-audit without shareholder approval, and waivers must be renewed annually. For ISIC 6201 software contracts, counterparties or lenders may contractually require an audited financial statement even when the statutory audit is waived.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Reporting issuers must apply International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS, CPA Canada Handbook Part I); private business corporations may elect Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) or IFRS. Annual financial statements must be prepared, approved by the board, and retained even in the absence of an audit; the CRA T2 corporate return reconciles book net income under the elected framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec Bill 195 (beneficial ownership transparency) requires the annual REQ update to identify every 'qualified beneficiary' — an individual who owns or controls 25% or more of the corporation's shares or votes, holds de facto control, or has the right to elect or remove a majority of directors. Share transfers that alter beneficial ownership must be reflected in the next annual update, and material UBO changes must be declared via an interim REQ update within 30 days. For a CBCA-incorporated entity, the internal Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be corrected within 15 days of any change and disclosed to the Canada Revenue Agency and prescribed enforcement bodies on demand. An annual internal 'register audit' should reconcile the share register, ISC register and director register against the REQ declaration before the filing deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (and senior officers, where maintained)
Minute Book containing shareholder and board resolutions and meeting minutes
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (CBCA ISC register; equivalently the REQ beneficial-ownership attestation file)
Register of share transfers and share allotments (with issue price and date)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–900 per year (CAD 200–1,200); lower end for a simple Quebec registered-office address rental, upper end for a full corporate agent including annual filing preparation, mail-forwarding and minute-book custody.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000–20,000 (CAD 9,500–27,000) for a full statutory audit of a remote desktop / IoT telemetry software company (ISIC 6201); USD 2,500–6,000 for a review engagement; USD 800–2,000 for a notice-to-reader compilation, each recurring annually when not waived.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate (Federal Part I 15% + Quebec general rate 11.5%). After the 10% federal provincial abatement on income allocated to a Quebec permanent establishment, the effective combined rate on active business income is approximately 16.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: first CA$500,000 of active business income eligible for a combined Federal + Quebec reduced rate of approximately 8.5% to 12.4%, depending on ownership and related corporation aggregation. Specific Quebec refundable tax credits for R&D (SR&ED-equivalent), innovation, e-business, and systematic software development may further reduce the effective rate. Accelerated Capital Cost Allowance (CCA) and immediate expensing allowances for eligible software assets and IoT equipment are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (filed through CRA EFILE/NETFILE using approved tax preparation software) and Quebec CO-17 (filed electronically via Revenu Québec's online filing system, generally integrated with the T2 transmission).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; large corporations and CCPCs may also be required to remit quarterly corporate income tax instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 and CO-17 must be filed no later than 6 months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., a December 31, 2024 year-end must be filed by June 30, 2025). The final balance of federal and Quebec income tax is due no later than 2 months after the fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months after for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity: legal name, Business Number (BN), Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), registered office address, jurisdiction of incorporation, fiscal year end, and effective date of dissolution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and directors must ensure the BN/NEQ block correctly identifies the corporation and any registered permanent establishment in Quebec; a non-resident corporation carrying on material remote-support/IoT activities through a server, office, or employees in Quebec must file a Quebec branch information schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before abatement; includes worldwide revenues from subscription software, remote desktop access, IoT data services, and installation or configuration fees, net of allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expressly disclose all income from Canadian clients, including cloud-based remote screen-share services, and determine whether the income is exempt under a tax treaty as business income absent a permanent establishment. File all relevant schedules and preserve geolocation/subscription records to substantiate the PE analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal provincial abatement for income allocated to Quebec, generally 10% of taxable income earned in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the T2 provincial allocation schedule and complete Quebec allocation on Revenu Québec's schedule based on the amount of Qualis Services rendered in Quebec and the location of servers/IoT telemetry flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal taxable income after loss carryovers, deductions, credits, and prior year adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Consolidate all tax-loss carryover positions; non-residents with historical Canadian losses cannot use prior-year losses unless the corporation maintains a Canadian taxable presence or treaty-protected property.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after the federal-provincial harmonization adjustments, including the adjustment for Quebec' s 'income tax (QST) remuneration' deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record Quebec net taxable income attributable to a permanent establishment. If the remote screen-share/IoT business does not create a Quebec PE, indicate no Quebec taxable income and prepare a documented PE-risk memorandum.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T2S(T/W) / Revenu Québec EDD Schedule (loss carry-forward)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trial balance of taxable capital gains, allowable capital losses, non-capital losses, and the specific line where non-capital losses are carried forward to offset current-year income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry forward losses only to the extent of the corporation's Canadian taxable income; substantial loss usage in a year with no structural presence may trigger CRA/Revenu Québec anti-avoidance inquiries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the balance owing, plus 1% per complete month for up to 12 months (maximum 17%). A repeated failure attracts 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Late payment interest is compounded daily at the prescribed rate. Revenu Québec adds parallel late-filing penalties up to 8% plus monthly surcharges, and a persistent failure to file may lead to additional disciplinary penalties and criminal exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax on non-resident dividends paid or credited by a Canadian-resident corporation, subject to reduction under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced treaty withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete and provide Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Relief under a Tax Convention) to the Canadian payer before payment. The payer must hold the Form NR301 to support the reduced rate. The non-resident must also obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority and, if requested, furnish it to the Canadian payer; an equivalent declaration under a limited time condition applies where the TRC cannot be obtained before payment. Revenu Québec does not administer a separate treaty relief mechanism; the reduced rate flows through the federal Part XIII withholding framework.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 25% absent treaty relief. Under the Canada-United States treaty, arm's-length interest is generally exempt from Canadian withholding (0%) and most patent, trademark, and copyright royalties are limited to 10%; under many other DTAs (e.g., with European states) royalty rates are 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on IP character and ownership structure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 must be filed with the T2 return where the aggregate value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions with a single non-resident party exceeds CA$1,000,000 during the taxation year. OECD-aligned Local File and Master File documentation should be prepared contemporaneously for any material inter-affiliate arrangement; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not impose a general Economic Substance Regulation framework (unlike UAE/offshore regimes), but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR), Quebec anti-avoidance rules, and treaty Limitation-on-Benefits/Principal Purpose Test provisions require real economic substance, actual headquarters, decision-making personnel, and meaningful ownership of IP and IoT software infrastructure. A 'shell' with a letterbox director and no Canadian activity will be disregarded for attribution and treaty entitlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Corporate Income Tax Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting international subscription revenue recorded by cloud/IoT payment platforms (Stripe/Paddle), fabricating R&D expenses, claiming SR&ED credits without genuine R&D activity, or failing to file the T2/CO-17 while still generating revenues through a Quebec permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalties from 25% to 50% of the understated federal/Quebec tax, plus late-filing penalties and interest; criminal conviction for tax evasion carries fines of up to CA$5,000 per offence and imprisonment for up to 5 years. Revenu Québec may impose separate fines under the Taxation Act and additional administrative penalties for assisted non-filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who approved false filings are jointly and severally liable for unremitted corporate income taxes, withheld payroll remittances, QST/GST, and withholdings on non-resident payments. The CRA and Revenu Québec can issue tax evasion penalties personally and, on criminal conviction, a court may order restitution, travel bans, and terms of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Quebec-incorporated shell company to route remote screen-share and IoT subscription fees from Canadian end-users to a head-office in a low-tax jurisdiction, with no employees, no decision-making, no server infrastructure, and no substantive R&D in Quebec, while claiming the Canada-resident status exclusively for treaty or provincial credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterization under GAAR, denial of dividend and royalty treaty benefits, 10%-20% GAAR penalties, reassessment of under-reported income, and a directive that the corporation disclose all ultimate beneficial ownership. CRA sections 207.4 and 247 can add penalties for failure to file prescribed information; treaty relief can be withdrawn, causing the 25% statutory withholding to apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who tolerate the shell structure may be personally liable for unremitted taxes, considered to have participated in 'culpable negligence', and can be named in comparable penalties plus disgorgement of funds paid to shell shareholders; time served in jail for deliberate tax facilitation may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting substantial business reseller payments or subscription fees without adequate know-your-business controls, allowing the remote IoT platform to be used by sanctioned shell clients, failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records required under Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act if the corporation falls under a reporting entity category, or using payment processors (Stripe/Paddle) to obscure ultimate revenue recipients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC penalties of up to CA$500,000 per administrative violation for registered reporting entities; criminal charges under the Criminal Code for laundering proceeds can result in fines of up to CA$2,000,000 and imprisonment for 10 years. A compliance failure may also trigger CRA audit and seizure of books and records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for AML penalties solely for directorship, but knowingly directing or encouraging an ultimate-designated money-laundering scheme leads to criminal liability, personal fines, travel restrictions, confiscation orders, and imprisonment up to 10 years. Promotion offences and false statements expose directors directly.
